Print the lot number on the replacement label before you peel the old one off, so the vial is never unlabelled. If you peeled first, there would be a moment when the vial had no identification. A distraction, a dropped label or a mix-up on the bench could then leave you with a vial you cannot positively identify. Printing first means you can copy the number while the original is still attached and check the new label against it before the swap.

Keep the peeled label with the paper record until the supervisor signs, because it is the only independent evidence of what the vial said before relabelling. The supervisor compares the lot number on the old label with the one on the new label to confirm it was transcribed correctly. If the old label were thrown away, any copying error would go unnoticed and could not be traced back.
